qa.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to Wheaton unit 8?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx , sheet Operating, lists generators WHT09, WHT10, WHT11, WHT12 and WHT13 at plant 4014. Each is a 9.8 MW natural gas internal combustion engine, operating October 2025. Together they are 49 MW, matching unit 8's five engines of 9.8 MW.
qa.recommendation: Record EIA ids WHT09 to WHT13 under Other IDs (unit) for unit 8, and WHT08 for unit 7. Generators 1 to 4 are the retired 1973 gas turbines of 48.5 MW, not unit 8.
qa.note: Generator 1, 2, 3 and 4 show retirement in May 2025. They are older units not in this record. The state utility filing on the Wisconsin Public Service Commission case page https://psc.wi.gov/Pages/CommissionActions/CasePages/WheatonRICEProject.aspx describes the repowering of the plant.

qa.question: Should the Environmental Integrity Project under construction row for Wheaton be ignored?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx shows unit 6 retired in January 2024 and the repowering units 7 to 13 operating. So the under construction label is stale.
qa.recommendation: Leave unit 6 as retired and unit 7 and 8 as operating.
qa.note: The Environmental Integrity Project page https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/rec_d4f1u68q7easr8ra1gcg did not load text I could check, so I did not read its source documents. I did not look for a link to older units 1 to 4, which EIA shows retired in May 2025 and which GEM has no record of.

qa.question: Should retired Wheaton units 1 to 4 be added to GEM?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 1 to 4 as natural gas combustion turbines of 48.5 MW, operating 1973, retired May 2025. GEM has no units for them.
qa.recommendation: Check whether they were earlier removed on purpose; they retired after 2020 so adding them as retired is allowed.
qa.note: Utility filings say the new plant replaces units 1 to 6. I found no filing that gives start years or owners for units 1 to 4 beyond the EIA table.
